questions.stem: What is the key difference between an indicative abstract and an informative abstract?

options.A: An indicative abstract reports detailed findings, while an informative abstract only outlines the scope
options.B: An indicative abstract tells the reader what the document discusses without reporting detailed findings, while an informative abstract provides the purpose, method, findings, and conclusion
options.C: An indicative abstract is always written by the author, while an informative abstract is always written by an indexer
options.D: An indicative abstract must appear under headings, while an informative abstract never does

questions.explanation: The indicative abstract answers 'What does this document discuss?', whereas the informative abstract gives substantive information including findings.

questions.stem: How does a critical abstract differ from an author's abstract?

options.A: A critical abstract is written by the author, while an author's abstract is written by an independent abstractor
options.B: A critical abstract only lists keywords, while an author's abstract summarises the content
options.C: A critical abstract offers an assessment of the document's strengths, weaknesses, methodology, reliability, or significance, while an author's abstract is prepared by the author of the original document
options.D: There is no difference; the two terms mean the same thing

questions.explanation: A critical abstract goes beyond description to evaluate the work (usually by someone with subject expertise); an author's abstract is simply one the document's own author prepared.

options.A: An abstract organised under clear headings such as Background, Objective, Method, Results, and Conclusion
options.B: An abstract that reports only the conclusions of the study, with no summary of the method
options.C: An abstract written by the author of the original document rather than by an independent indexer or abstractor
options.D: An abstract that emphasises the particular aspects of a document that are most relevant to a specific audience

questions.explanation: A slant abstract emphasises the aspects of a document most relevant to a specific audience — the source may be presented differently for each kind of reader.

questions.stem: Which set lists the common headings used in a structured abstract?

options.A: Background, Objective, Method, Results, and Conclusion

questions.explanation: A structured abstract organises content under clear headings such as Background, Objective, Method, Results, and Conclusion, which improves scanning.

questions.stem: Which is a quality of a good abstract?

options.A: It includes unsupported claims to make the study sound important
options.B: It is clear, concise, accurate, objective, self-contained, coherent, grammatically correct, and faithful to the source document
options.C: It adds the personal opinions of the person writing it
options.D: It introduces invented information missing from the source

questions.explanation: Good abstracts are clear, concise, accurate, objective, self-contained, coherent, grammatically correct, and faithful to the source — never unsupported or invented content.
